hints.title: Recover the original roots
hints.body: Since x2+bx+c is negative exactly between p and q, p and q are its roots. Consequently p+q=−b and pq=c.
hints.recap: A monic quadratic is determined by the sum and product of its roots.

hints.title: Construct the transformed quadratic
hints.body: The numbers cp and cq have sum c(p+q)=−bc and product c2pq=c3. These match x2+bcx+c3.
hints.recap: Build a new quadratic from the transformed root sum and product.
hints.pitfall: Scaling both roots by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> multiplies their product by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.

hints.title: Order the new boundaries
hints.body: Use the negative sign of c to decide which transformed root is smaller. Then use the sign of the leading coefficient to decide where the new quadratic is negative.
hints.recap: Multiplying an inequality by a negative number reverses its direction.
hints.pitfall: The root order may reverse when both roots are multiplied by a negative number.
hints.pause: Write the interval in increasing order, choosing the correct endpoint inclusion.

recall.reminder: Multiplying an inequality by a negative number reverses its direction.

solution:
The original quadratic has roots p and q, so p+q=−b and pq=c. Hence (x−cp)(x−cq)=x2−c(p+q)x+c2pq=x2+bcx+c3.

The transformed quadratic therefore has roots cp and cq. As p<q and c<0, their order is cq<cp. Its leading coefficient is positive, so it is negative exactly between them.

The answer is cq<x<cp, option D. The endpoints are excluded because the requested inequality is strict.
knowledgePattern: Scale a quadratic inequality by a negative root parameter
